items.title: This Bengaluru Startup Is Launching Disney-Inspired Robots In The US And Japan First
items.summary: Bengaluru-based Eyecandy Robotics is structuring its studio like Pixar or Walt Disney, animating physical-world characters instead of pixels on a screen. Anchored in reinforcement learning (RL) and human-robot interaction (HRI), the team trains small, desktop-friendly bots in simulation to move with distinct emotions, personalities, and low-latency physical reflexes. In this exclusive hacker house walkthrough for Tech Talks, Senior Tech Journalist Siddharth Jindal visits Eyecandy Robotics in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, to sit down with Co-Founder Mankaran Singh. Along with co-founders Raghav and Alama, Singh demonstrates Disney-inspired BDX droids and consumer prototypes Pico and Tensor. He explains why reinforcement learning outperforms generic LLMs for real-time robotic reactions, navigating B2B theme park licensing deals, consumer market strategies across the US and Japan, 3D printing and custom motor engineering, and overcoming hardware manufacturing bottlenecks in India. Can entertainment robotics bridge the gap to consumer adoption long before general-purpose humanoids enter our homes?
